faculty.name: Ms. Jasmin A. Arani
faculty.biography:
My work focuses on the phytochemical characterization, pharmacological potential, and profiling of Actinodaphne malabarica N.P. Balakr medicinal plant species.

Through this research, I evaluate the plant's chemical compounds and test their therapeutic properties to unlock its medicinal value.

In addition to laboratory research, I actively educate postgraduate (M.Sc.) students in advanced botanical sciences.

Ultimately, my efforts bridge the gap between plant taxonomy, ecological conservation, and modern pharmacological science.

faculty.name: Mr. Venkatesh Jugal
faculty.biography: A research scholar in Applied Botany, specializing in plant ecology, biodiversity, and molecular phylogeny, with doctoral research focused on the genus *Nothopegia* Blume, an endemic and ecologically significant tree genus of the Western Ghats. My research explores the diversity, distribution, and ecological relationships of Nothopegia species, emphasizing the influence of climatic and edaphic factors on their distribution across the Central Western Ghats of Karnataka. My work integrates field-based ecological investigations, vegetation analysis, soil and climatic assessments, and molecular techniques to understand species relationships and evolutionary patterns. Alongside my research, I am interested in plant taxonomy, forest ecology, phytochemistry, medicinal plants, and biodiversity conservation, with a broader commitment to understanding plant–environment interactions and contributing to the conservation of the unique flora of the Western Ghats.
faculty.research_interests: Molecular phylogeny and Taxonomy and bio geography
faculty.academic_journey: Msc in Botany 2021 in Davangere University
faculty.research_summary: Diversity distribution and molecular phylogeny of genus Nothopegia in central western Ghats, Karnataka

faculty.name: Dr. Santhosh K. Hanumanthappa
faculty.biography: My research focuses on multidisciplinary work such as Natural product-based drug discovery, Nanobiotechnology, Biomaterials, and Environmental biotechnology. I identified β-keto amyrin, a natural compound from Cryptostegia grandiflora as a potent inhibitor of Daboia russellii venom phospholipase A₂, demonstrating significant anti-inflammatory potential. I also established the antiproliferative and antioxidant activities of C. grandiflora leaf extract. I guide master’s student projects. I have developed Brugmansia suaveolens-conjugated chitosan nanoparticles with enhanced antioxidant and antibacterial properties. My work includes engineering sardine fish-derived chitosan–collagen hybrid membranes as novel wound-healing scaffolds and developing Curcuma xanthorrhiza-doped chitosan–hydroxyapatite biomaterials for disrupting bacterial communication and biofilms. Additionally, I investigated hydrocarbon biodegradation by soil microorganisms and quorum-quenching actinomycetes for environmental remediation and combating antimicrobial resistance.

faculty.name: Prof. H. S. Santosh Kumar
faculty.biography:
I am a Professor in the Department of Studies and Research in Biotechnology at Kuvempu University, Karnataka. My research bridges computational biology, systems biology, and computer-aided drug design (CADD), with a focus on resolving complex biomedical challenges.

My investigative work centers on multi-omic big data analysis, transcriptomic profiling, interactomics, and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate disease pathways and discover novel therapeutic targets. Key directions include identifying biomarkers for inflammatory conditions and gastric malignancies, tackling antimicrobial resistance mechanisms in pathogens like Helicobacter pylori, and characterizing natural product inhibitors and bioactive peptides.

With over two decades of academic and research experience, I have authored numerous peer-reviewed publications and mentored postgraduate and doctoral scholars. I am deeply committed to advancing data-driven biotechnology, integrating modern cheminformatics with wet-lab insights to translate biological data into actionable biomedical solutions.
faculty.research_interests: Rosetta stones, Metagenomics, Inflammation markers, CADD, Systems biology

faculty.biography: My research focuses on comparative genomics, pathogen drug target characterization, and high-throughput virtual screening using grid-computing platforms to identify novel therapeutic inhibitors. I investigate essential microbial proteins and pathways across bacterial pathogens like Helicobacter pylori and streptococci, pairing reductive genomics with molecular docking and dynamic simulations to evaluate synthetic and natural scaffolds. faculty.name: Ms. Sneha M. A. Anthony
faculty.biography:
My research focuses on the synthesis of heterocyclic compounds through green catalytic approaches and conventional organic synthetic methodologies, with particular emphasis on exploring their potential biological applications. I am also actively involved in the synthesis and development of agrochemically important molecules, particularly isoxazolones, and investigating their potential applications as herbicidal, pesticidal, and fungicidal agents.

In addition to my research activities, I serve as a full-time Lecturer in the Postgraduate Department of Chemistry, where I teach and mentor Master's students. I am passionate about creating a supportive and student-friendly academic environment, providing guidance not only in academic development but also in students' overall well-being. I strongly believe in approachable teaching, effective communication, and student counselling to help learners manage academic challenges and stress while developing confidence and independent thinking.

Beyond my regular teaching responsibilities, I actively conduct coaching classes for competitive examinations, particularly KSET and CSIR-UGC NET, to support students aspiring to pursue careers in higher education and research.

I am enthusiastic about academic and research collaborations within my areas of expertise and welcome opportunities for interdisciplinary research and teaching initiatives. I am particularly interested in collaborative projects that integrate organic synthesis, green chemistry, medicinal chemistry, biological sciences, and agricultural sciences to address scientific challenges and contribute to sustainable development.

I, Vasanthanaik P, am a dedicated teacher with over three years of experience in promoting fitness, sportsmanship, and a healthy lifestyle among students. I hold a Bachelor’s degree (B.P.Ed.) and a Master’s degree (M.P.Ed.) in Physical Education, along with certifications in First Aid and sports training.

I possess expertise in organizing school sports events, athletics training, and yoga sessions, as well as team sports such as football, cricket, volleyball, and basketball. I successfully train school teams for district and state-level competitions, helping students develop discipline, teamwork, and self-confidence.

faculty.name: Ms. Vasudha S. S.
faculty.biography: Track and field is considered the mother of all sports, where performance is a complex interaction of body structure and physical capacities. Success in sprints, jumps, throws and middle-distance events is not by chance but determined by specific morphological and fitness profiles. Hence, deciphering these variables is essential for talent identification and training optimization.
faculty.research_interests: Sports and physical education, Human morphology, physical fitness , psychology

faculty.biography: My work focuses on photosynthesis, photorespiration and how plants respond to warming. Alongside teaching and developing university-wide courses, I support researchers across disciplines through training in digital tools and advanced research methods. I guide PhD and master’s student projects and contribute to long-term forest monitoring and photosynthetic heat-tolerance measurements in Bhadra Reserve Forest, alongside related field and laboratory collaborations in Goa and elsewhere.

faculty.name: Dr. Preema Karal Andrade
faculty.biography: A Biotechnology researcher and academician with a PhD focused on predicting protein–ligand interaction networks and validating their biological significance in cancer cell lines. My work bridges computational biology, bioinformatics, and experimental molecular research, with interests in cancer biology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, transcriptomics, and genomic data analysis. I have also gained hands-on experience in bioinformatics through an internship at Molsys, involving NGS and exome data analysis, variant annotation, transcriptomics, and genomic data interpretation. Alongside my research, I am actively involved in teaching and academic mentoring, currently serving as a Guest Lecturer in the Department of Food Technology at Kuvempu University.
faculty.academic_journey: PhD in Cancer Biology, Kuvempu University (2023); MSc in Biotechnology, Kuvempu University (2018); BSc in Zoology, Biotechnology, Chemistry, Sahyadri Science College (2016)

faculty.name: Ms. Aishwarya M.
faculty.biography: A Food Technology academic and researcher currently working as a Guest Lecturer in the Department of Food Technology at Kuvempu University, Karnataka, and a UGC-NET qualified candidate in Home Science. I completed my M.Sc. in Food Technology from Kuvempu University in 2024 and my B.Sc. from Smt. Indira Gandhi Government First Grade Women's College in 2022. My postgraduate research focused on the development of edible cutlery using millet flour, with an emphasis on nutritional composition and sensory evaluation, exploring sustainable and biodegradable alternatives to conventional plastic-based food service materials. My research interests include millet-based value-added food product development, food preservation and processing technologies, functional foods and nutraceuticals, sustainable food packaging, edible films and coatings, food safety, and nutritional evaluation of innovative food products. I am particularly interested in developing nutritious, sustainable, and innovative food solutions through research and technological advancements in food science.
faculty.research_interests: Millet based value added food product development, Sustainable food packaging, Edible films and coatings, Functional foods and nutraceuticals, Food preservation and processing technologies
faculty.academic_journey: MSc in Food Technology (2024); BSc in CBZ (2022)

faculty.name: Dr. Sachin S. Nayaka
faculty.biography: A researcher and academician at Kuvempu University, Karnataka, with expertise in biotechnology, phytochemistry, pharmacology, and food technology. His research focuses on medicinal plant-based bioactive compounds, sustainable food packaging, biopolymer development, and environmental applications. He has over four years of research experience as a DBT-Senior Research Fellow and is actively involved in teaching, postgraduate research supervision, and interdisciplinary scientific research. He has guided 20 M.Sc. students, published several research articles, and received prestigious recognitions, including the Young Scientist Award (2025) and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Young Academic Excellence Award (2026), Best Food-tech Innovation Award (2026) and Excellence of Research Award (2026). Also my work emphasizes scientific innovation, sustainable development, and the application of biological resources for societal and environmental well-being.
faculty.research_interests: Phytochemistry, Pharmacology, Bioprocess technology, Molecular biology, Immunology, Microbiology

faculty.name: Prof. Chandrashekar E.
faculty.biography: My academic focus encompasses Policy Planning, Rural Studies, and Community Development, areas in which he has made significant contributions through research, publications, and academic service. My research in policy planning examines the formulation and implementation of policies aimed at addressing social issues and promoting sustainable development. I work in rural studies explores the socio-economic conditions of rural communities, focusing on aspects such as agriculture, education, and infrastructure. I research in community development emphasizes the empowerment of local communities through participatory approaches and capacity-building initiatives. I'm authored numerous research articles and books related to these areas, contributing to the academic discourse on rural development and community empowerment. i serves as an editorial member and reviewer for several internationally reputable journals, reflecting his active engagement with the global academic community, has held various academic and administrative positions, including serving as the Convener of the Committee for the Commemorative Volume on the Silver Jubilee Year of the Karnataka Sociology Association (KSA), demonstrating his leadership and commitment to the academic community. I has been involved in curriculum development and has served as a member of various Boards of Studies and Doctoral Committees across multiple universities, contributing to the shaping of sociology education in the region.
